newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee edges to new six-week high at close.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee edges to new six-week high at close.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices edged to a fresh six-week high Friday, as supply jitters continued to bolster the spot December contract, trading sources said.

Aided by good buying interest from commission houses and commodity funds, coffee prices hovered in positive territory throughout the session. Scattered selling from producer countries provided some resistance, but overall participation by the industry was limited, traders said.
Benchmark December futures climbed 1.40 cent a lb on the day, to 116.30, settling just shy of the intraday peak of 116.80.
Concern that this year's Latin American harvest, hampered by severe rains, was getting off to a slow start continued to underpin prices, said Smith Barney analyst Walter Spilka.
"The crop is slow in coming in," he said. "The (market) psychology has changed back to bullish."

But with the supply scenario expected to improve by late 1996, the deferred positions could continue to lose ground to spot December, he said. December's already hefty premium to March rose by a further 0.75 cent a lb Friday, to 8.65 cents.

In other news, Colombia's truck drivers announced Friday they would stage a nationwide strike beginning next week. While traders said there was some concern the work stoppage could slow exports from the country, the news had little immediate impact on prices.

Views that the recent bull run may have been exaggerated could provoke a sudden technical retracement next week, several traders said, adding that they would be paying close attention to tonight's Commitment of Traders data. Technically, December faces resistance at today's high of 116.80, followed by 118.25, dealers said. Support was noted at 115.10 and 114.30.
Volume on the exchange was steady Friday, at an estimated 6,850 lots.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
